the traditional view is that table instances must respect all functional

with a truth value among the following: true, false, inconsistent or unknown;
and we show that our framework can be used to study important problems such as
consistent query answering, table merging, and data quality measures - to
mention just a few. In this paper, however, we focus mainly on consistent query
answering, a problem that has received considerable attention during the last
decades.

approach to handle inconsistencies in a table with nulls and functional
dependencies, (b) we give algorithms for computing all true, inconsistent and

solution to the consistent query answering problem and compare our solution to
that of table repairs.

important problems can be studied.

and the merging of two tables with nulls and functional dependencies.

atmospheric monitoring for optical
experiments in high-energy astrophysics is seemingly straightforward, but
reaching high precision of the density measurements is challenging. One of the
key problems is the effect of correlated noise due to the finite field-of-view
of the photometers. We developed a novel approach based on the generalized
method of correlated charm to take this effect into account. This approach
provides a direct way to calculate the noise contribution from the random
variability of the sky background and the detector nonlinearity. It is valid
for any distribution of the sky background and takes into account the
correlations between photons separated by any distance. The method is
general and can be applied to any photometric measurement in optical and
near-ultraviolet wavebands.
  Using simulated data, we tested the approach on sky background measurements
with different configurations of photometers (various solid angles, signals,
and nonlinearity strengths) and background scenarios (different average
intensities and variability spectra). The results are in excellent agreement
with the theoretical expectations derived from the model. The model allows us
to accurately predict the shape of the autocorrelation function, the
momentum-based variance, and the correct scaling of the dispersion in the
autocorrelation plot. The maximum possible precision is in the range of 0.5% to
1% for typical quick look systems in optical experiments.
  The method is valid for up to 10% of nonlinearity, corresponding to strong
sources (e.g., Moon) in the field-of-view or very weak quick look systems.
Overestimation of the standard deviation is demonstrated for a field-of-view
larger than $10^\circ$, which helps in avoiding overestimation of the density
in practice. The approach is independent of the background variability spectrum,
which is an advantage over other methods. Although the scope of this work was
focused on atmospheric monitoring, the method can be applied to any
photometric measurement.
  Testing the approach on real data would allow us to assess its reliability on
actual atmospheric monitoring data. Further development of the method will
include applying it to real data and investigating its limitations on
atmospheric density measurements.

convolutional neural network (CNN) has received considerable attention.
Depending on whether intermediate cues are used, the relevant literature can be
roughly divided into two broad categories: direct methods and two stage
pipelines. For the latter, intermediate cues, such as 3D object coordinates,
semantic keypoints, or virtual control points instead of pose parameters are
regressed by CNN in the first stage. Object pose can then be solved by
correspondence constraints constructed with these intermediate cues. In this
paper, we focus on the postprocessing of a two-stage pipeline and propose to
combine two learning concepts for estimating object pose under challenging
scenes: projection grouping on one side, and correspondence learning on the
other. We firstly employ a local patch based method to predict projection
heatmaps which denote the confidence distribution of projection of 3D bounding
box's corners. A projection grouping module is then proposed to remove
redundant local maxima from each layer of heatmaps. Instead of directly feeding
2D-3D correspondences to the perspective-n-point (PnP) algorithm, multiple
correspondence hypotheses are sampled from local maxima and its corresponding
neighborhood and ranked by a correspondence-evaluation network. Finally,
correspondences with higher confidence are selected to determine object pose.
Extensive experiments on three public datasets demonstrate that the proposed
framework outperforms several state-of-the-art methods, especially under
cluttered scenes.

stability problem for a
stretched Euler--Bernoulli beam on a star-shaped metric graph with three
identical edges. The edges are hinged with respect to the outer vertices. The
inner vertex is capable of both translation and rotation, the latter of which
is subject to a combination of elastic and frictional effects. We present
detailed results on the asymptotic distribution and structure of the spectrum
of the linear operator associated with the abstract spectral problem in Hilbert
space. Within this framework it is shown that the eigenvectors have the
property of forming an unconditional or Riesz basis, which makes it possible to
directly deduce the exponential stability of the corresponding $C_0$-semigroup.
As an aside it is shown that the particular choice of connectivity conditions
ensures exponential stability even when the elasticity acting on the slopes of the
edges is absent.
  The main contribution of this paper is to establish the connection between
this particular class of spectral problems and a system of ordinary differential
equations with periodic coefficients. This connection is then exploited to
accurately determine the asymptotic distribution of the eigenvalues. It is shown
that the eigenvalues are asymptotically equally spaced on the imaginary axis,
with the approximation order depending on the length of the edges as well as the
values of the slopes. Due to the unconditional basis property of the eigenvectors
the approximation order is then translated to the approximation order of the
exponential stability rate in the space $l_2$.
  The structure of the spectrum is such that the eigenvalues come in sequences
with equally spaced imaginary parts, which is conditioned by the conservation
law inherent in the system describing the dynamics of the slopes. Due to the
periodicity of the system's matrix, its trace is known in advance, and the

  Our goal is to minimize the number and complexity of hardware and software
components that a smartphone owner needs to trust to withstand adversarial
inputs. We present a multi-domain hardware design composed of
statically-partitioned, physically-isolated trust domains that communicate
throughfully-verifiable, zero-caps exchange channels. To enforce the hardware
partitioning, we introduce a novel, fine-grained, performance-competitive
operating system design that consists of multiple independently-installed,
untrusted "oslets" -- each with its own device drivers, running on untrusted
Isa extensions -- that communicate through a verifiable, inter-oslet
communication API. The oslets are responsible for providing services to
applications, such as process and thread management, memory allocation, and
I/O. A small, highly-trusted "rootlet" manages the hardware description
consisting of multiple (non-overlapping) trust domains, and provides a
communication interface to the oslets. The oslets, oslet APIs, and hardware
description are verified in Coq.
  We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach by implementing a
prototypical hardware design and an operating system for it. Our results
demonstrate that the resulting hardware and software can provide a
programmable ISA extension that enforces hardware partitions with
inter-partition communication channels that are guaranteed to not share
hardware resources and to follow a fully-verifiable communication protocol.
The cost of the communication is minimal -- around 3-4 CPU cycles per
communication operation. The cost of the hardware support for our multi-domain
design is also minimal -- around 1.7KB of L1 cache.
  Overall, our work provides a novel multi-domain hardware and a performance-
competitive operating system that can help reduce the trusted compute base in
a system. It can be used to generate security-critical programs that run in a
sandbox that is enforced by the hardware and the operating system. This can
assist in detecting and containing malware that could be written to "escape"
the sandbox.
  We hope this work will inspire further research in exploring hardware
designs that can enforce multiple, mutually-distrustful domains with
inter-domain communication channels that are guaranteed to follow a fully-
verifiable communication protocol.

located in complex reservoir formations. To effectively produce from such
reservoirs and reduce costs, optimized well placement in real-time
(geosteering) is crucial. Geosteering is usually assisted by an updated
formation evaluation obtained by well-log interpretation while drilling. A
reliable, computationally efficient, and robust workflow to interpret well logs
and capture uncertainties in real-time is necessary for this application. An
iterative ensemble-based method, namely the approximate Levenberg Marquardt
form of the Ensemble Randomized Maximum Likelihood (LM-EnRML) is integrated in
our formation evaluation workflow. We estimate model parameters, resistivity
and density in addition to boundary locations, and related uncertainties by
reducing the statistical misfit between the measurements from the well logging
tools and the theoretical measurements from the forward tool simulators. The
results of analyzing several synthetic cases with several types of logs
verified that the proposed method can give good estimate of model parameters.
  By comparing the CPU time, we conclude that the proposed method has at least
about 10--125 times lower computational time compare to a common statistical
method, such as Metropolis-Hastings Monte Carlo. In addition, the
ensemble-based method can run in parallel on multiple CPUs. Testing the method
on a case inspired by a real field is also presented. The obtained results
are in good agreement with the industry-standard software.
  In conclusion, the proposed method can give accurate formation evaluation
and predict uncertainties related to well-log interpretation in real-time
geosteering application. Reducing the misfit between the theoretical and
measured data by incorporating higher order tools such as density logs and
calculating uncertainties by utilizing large number of ensemble members are
two important features of this study. These two features make this study
relevant to accurately determine poorly conducting and poorly consolidating
rock formations, e.g. shales. With increasing number of wells to be geosteered
in real-time, our method will be important to run in parallel to increase the
efficiency and reduce the costs of the operation.
  Finally, our method is important for the future study of quantifying the
impact of uncertainty of formation properties on the well performance.
Moreover, integrating our method with the reservoir simulation in parallel with
the geosteering process will be crucial for that purpose.

extraction techniques, named entity recognition (NER) is widely used to extract
information from texts for downstream tasks. Nested NER is a branch of NER in
which the named entities (NEs) are nested with each other. However, most of the
previous studies on nested NER usually apply linear structure to model the
nested NEs which are actually accommodated in a hierarchical structure. Thus in
order to address this mismatch, this work models the hierarchical NEs in a
hierarchical structure and we propose a new methodology named Hierarchical
Named-Entity Representation (HNER) to handle them. In HNER, we propose the
concept of the first-level and second-level NEs to classify the nested NEs
into two types. Based on these two types of NEs, we design two types of labels
to annotate them separately. Then we propose a novel framework to extract them
automatically. Experiments show that HNER is on par or even better than the
state-of-the-art methods in Chinese nested NER. Moreover, the proposed HNER
framework is applied to Korean nested NER and it achieves similar performance to
the state-of-the-art methods in Korean NER tasks.

tropical geometric objects in the product whose factors weigh the ways they

distinct geometric objects, and its contribution is not captured by the
tropical mass formula.

features along four dimensions and find that teachers convey similar semantic
concepts via spoken words for different conditions of (1) demonstration types,
(2) audio usage instructions, (3) subtasks, and (4) errors during

duration and expressiveness are present along the four dimensions, highlighting
that human audio carries rich information, potentially beneficial for
technological advancement of robot learning from demonstration methods.
Furthermore, we find that teachers are consistent in using certain audio
features across different demonstrations of the same task as well as overall.
These findings indicate that teachers have a preference for how they couple
manipulation demonstrations with audio, which is important for optimizing
interaction design of robot learning from demonstration interfaces.
Subsequently, we argue that robot learning from demonstration interaction
designs can effectively leverage audio cues by incorporating audio features
specific to human teacher feedback. This can lead to more efficient
demonstrations, better performance on varied test cases, and ultimately more

high performances on unprecedented data, large and diverse datasets must be
included during the training process.

present in the learning step, in particular by including more diverse data.

in order to be able to learn robust models across the whole spectrum of the

In this paper, we consider the multi-agent extension of the Motivation Dynamics
framework and show how the framework can be extended to encode persistent
multi-agent rendezvous behaviors. We analytically characterize the bifurcation
properties of the resulting system, and numerically show that it exhibits

  When compared to previous multi-agent rendezvous algorithms, our proposed
scheme has the advantage of not requiring explicit distance sensing between
agents. Instead, each agent uses only sensory input from its local flow field,
which can be provided by a network of mobile sensors acting under the same
motivation dynamics as the agents. This makes our multi-agent system more
scalable and flexible, as the steering behavior of each agent is not
sensitively dependent on the performance of any single sensor.
  Finally, we show how the bifurcation-based behavior of our multi-agent system
can be exploited to adapt the navigation of the agents (and sensors) in
response to bifurcations in the motivation dynamics. This allows the agents to
effectively "surf" the desired steady-state flows, resulting in simplified
steering while maintaining the benefit of not requiring direct agent-sensor
communication.

correlation between this and the Hubble diagram residuals of the supernovae has
$3.6\sigma$ significance, and is consistent with weak lensing magnification due

nuclear spin lifetimes. To date, these defect centres have only been studied as
ensembles in bulk silicon. Here, we demonstrate the reliable creation of high
concentration T centre ensembles in the 220 nm device layer of
silicon-on-insulator (SOI) wafers by ion implantation and subsequent annealing.

benchmark the characteristic optical spectral diffusion within these T centre
ensembles. Using this new technique, we show that with minimal optimization to
the fabrication process high densities of implanted T centres localized

total spectral diffusion.

integration with other solid-state technologies is considered. With the development
of post-processing fabrication techniques that can be applied to SOI wafers,
we demonstrate the feasibility of a future technology that can meet the
requirement for reliable, high-performance telecom photon-spin interfaces.

high-performance near-infrared solid-state qubit platforms, such as diamond.

a medical image processing technique that
used radio waves to scan the body. It is a tomographic imaging technique,
principally used in the field of radiology. With the advantage of being a
painless diagnostic procedure, MRI allows medical personnel to illustrate clear
pictures of the anatomy and the physiological processes occurring in the body,
thus allowing early detection and treatment of diseases. These images, combined
with image processing techniques may be used in the detection of tumors,
difficult to identify with the naked eye. This digital assignment surveys the
different image processing techniques used in Automated Tumor Detection (ATD).
This assignment initiates the discussion with a comparison of traditional
techniques such as Morphological Tools (MT) and Region Growing Technique (RGT).
It continues with the discussion of newer techniques such as Convolutional
Neural Networks (CNN), which are used in Deep Learning (DL). DL is a subfield
of machine learning that uses algorithms inspired by the structure and function
of the brain to perform tasks such as ATD. The assignment further discusses
different types of CNNs such as LeNet, CNN34 and ResNet34, and how they are
trained with thousands of images to evaluate the performance using metrics such
as Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Mean Squared Error (MSE). The assignment
concludes with a comparison of the techniques, highlighting the advantages and
disadvantages of each ATD method. It also emphasises the need for further
research, to develop more robust and efficient DL algorithms for ATD, to enable
the early detection of tumors in MRI images.

Range Sectoring, organizes sensors in different sectors based on their location
within the network. Based on this organization, nodes from each sector are

been implemented in TinyOS 2.1, and evaluated in a testbed using TelosB motes.

reliability, especially in large networks and in scenarios with bottlenecks.

efficient data collection, since it is able to reach the base station in a
short time. The evaluation of the two mechanisms have shown that they are
practical and can be effective to design other protocols for specific

sensitive task? Deep
object detectors exploit scene context for recognition differently. In this
paper, we group object detectors into 3 categories in terms of context use: no
context by cropping the input (RCNN), partial context by cropping the
featuremap (two-stage methods) and full context without any cropping
(single-stage methods). We systematically evaluate the effect of context for
each deep detector category. We create a fully controlled dataset for varying
context and investigate the context for deep detectors. We also evaluate
gradually removing the background context and the foreground object on MS COCO.
We demonstrate that single-stage and two-stage object detectors can and will
use the context by virtue of their large receptive field. Thus, choosing the
best object detector may depend on the application context.
  As this work demonstrates that single-stage and two-stage object detectors
exploit the context differently, it paves the way for a fully-fledged
theoretical analysis of the effect of context on deep object detectors.
  Further, we present a novel context evaluation framework that facilitates
comparative study of varying object detector architectures.

exact ergodic capacity (EC) of a
point-to-point multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) system assisted by an
intelligent reflecting surface (IRS). In addition, we account for the effects
of correlated Rayleigh fading and the intertwinement between the amplitude and
the phase shift of the reflecting coefficient of each IRS element, which are
usually both neglected despite their presence in practice. Random matrix theory
tools allow to derive the probability density function (PDF) of the cascaded
channel in closed form, and subsequently, the EC, which depend only on the
large-scale statistics and the phase shifts. Notably, we optimize the EC with
respect to the phase shifts with low overhead, i.e., once per several coherence
intervals instead of the burden of frequent necessary optimization required by
expressions being dependent on instantaneous channel information. Monte-Carlo
(MC) simulations verify the analytical results and demonstrate the insightful
interplay among the key parameters and their impact on the EC.
  Furthermore, we consider a extensions of the previous scenario by assuming that
a part of the transceivers are served by an IRS each, thus forming a multi-user
MIMO system. Again, the EC is derived in closed-form and optimized with respect
to the phase shifts of all IRSs with low overhead. MC simulations verify the
analytical results and show the impact of the increasing number of served users
and IRSs on the EC.
  In both scenarios, we also investigate the predictive overhead required to
approximate the EC with a high degree of accuracy. The results indicate that
lower overhead is required when the fading is uncorrelated compared to the
correlated case.

travelling chimera states in networks of phase oscillators.

and argue that there is still work in progress to develop a general theory of

waves and chimera states are more likely to occur. The underlying mathematics

accept updates without coordination with each other, and the updates are then
propagated asynchronously. This brings the critical challenge of conflict
resolution among concurrent updates. Conflict-free Replicated Data Type (CRDT)
is a principled approach to addressing this challenge. However, existing CRDT
designs are tricky, and hard to be generalized to other data types. A design
framework is in great need to guide the systematic design of new CRDTs.
  To address this challenge, we propose RWF -- the Remove-Win design Framework
for CRDTs. RWF leverages the simple but powerful remove-win strategy to resolve
conflicting updates, and provides generic design for a variety of data
container types. Two exemplar implementations following RWF are given over the
Redis data type store, which demonstrate the effectiveness of RWF. Performance
measurements of our implementations further show the efficiency of CRDT designs
following RWF.
  In addition, we propose a theoretical foundation for the design of RWF. We
classify conflicts in multi-node systems into three types -- lose-win, remove-win
and win-win -- and investigate the lower bound of the resolution cost of any
conflict resolution protocol. The theoretical foundation and the careful
engineering of RWF and its exemplars together contribute to the understanding of
the trade-offs in conflict resolution.

strategies for both the last leader and the last writer data types, and
implement the exemplar CRDTs following RWF. The performance of our implementations
further shows the efficiency of design of RWF.

eradicating spreads of malicious phenomena in networks, such as epidemics and
fake information, which are generally named in the research networks
immunization. The traditional approach of evaluating the effectiveness of
attacks on networks is focused on measuring the proportion of nodes in a system
that are infected by malicious phenomena, that is, the system's infection
ratio. However, in very large systems such as social networks with millions of
members, the infection ratio cannot fully characterize an systems' operation
phenomena, especially, diffusion ability of an system. Based on above
observations, we propose a new attack measure - an systems' diffusion ability,
which is defined by the maximum output of an system's degree distribution. Our
theoretical and empirical analyses show that the attack measure is able to
charaterize an systems' spreading behavior, and thus, is useful in evaluating
an systems' immunity ability, which is very important in networks immunization.
As a case study, we use the microblog system Weibo as an empirical example to
analyze the diffusion ability of social media based on their attack measures,
which are obtained via simulation. Our analysis indicates that the Chinese
government can adopt strategies of allowing more topics to flow through the
social media, which are currently blocked, in order to early discover and
control online attacks, such as spreading of false information related to the
Xinjiang conflict, the Hong Kong protest, and the new coronavirus disease 2019
(nCoV-19).
  We propose three strategies for an system to pursue lower attack measure, that
is, less spreading power, such as an social media to reduce spreading of false
information, and give corresponding analysis and case study by using the
microblog system Weibo as an empirical example. That is, an system can (1) trim
its tail of the degree distribution, (e.g., by deleting low-degree nodes),
which is called as trimming strategy; (2) shift its degree distribution to the
left, (e.g., by reassigning links to other nodes with lower degrees), which is
called as as shifting strategy; and (3) normalize its degree distribution, that
is, to be close to the uniform distribution, (e.g., by randomly exchanging
links with other nodes), which is called as a normalization strategy. Simulation
results on the dataset of Weibo show that these three strategies are effective
in decreasing an systems' diffusion ability as well as its infection ratio. Of

on a linear chain of trapped ions, using Gaussian amplitude modulation and a
constant laser frequency. We select this frequency to balance the entanglement
accumulation of all motional modes during the gate to produce a strong
robustness to frequency error, even for long ion chains. We demonstrate this
technique on a three-ion chain, achieving $<\,1\%$ reduction from peak fidelity
over a $20\,$kHz range of frequency offset, and we analyze the performance of
this gate design through numerical simulations on chains of two to 33 ions.
Through these numerical studies, we can produce gates that are resistant to
 heating, such that the total expected motional quenching is reduced by more
than a factor of 25 compared to traditional techniques, while maintaining
reasonable execution time ($\lesssim\,100\,\mu\mathrm{m}$).

values of motional parameters (e.g., masses, couplings) that yield the highest
frequency robustness, and we provide this design with numerical support through
simulations on chains of two to 33 ions.

of combined frequency and amplitude modulation, showing that it is the highest
performing frequency-resonant gate execution strategy (strategy that balances
the accumulation of motional phases among different normal modes during the
gate execution) in terms of robustness to heating, and we discuss the benefits
of this strategy within a multi-qubit quantum algorithm.
  With the techniques presented here, one can execute this gate on various
platforms, including the ones currently in operation, to achieve high
frequency robustness, or combine it with other advanced motion control schemes
to achieve the highest levels of overall robustness.

can strongly resist frequency and heating errors, allowing for the stable

Hidden Node Structure (GNN-HNS)" that can learn a node influence function and
estimate the direct and indirect effects in a given graph. The node influence
function learned by our proposed method can reflect not only the strength of
the direct connections between nodes but also the overall node influence
structure. We introduce two algorithms to infer the hidden node structure from
the observed graph, where the connections and the influence weights are
parameterized using Graph Neural Networks (GNN). We also present how to use the
node influence function to estimate the direct and indirect effects. We conduct
extensive experiments on real and synthetic datasets to evaluate the performance
of our proposed method. The results show that our method performs better than
some existing methods in estimating direct and indirect effects and learning

common concern raised from ex-post assessments is that storage resources can
fail to respond to strong price signals during times of scarcity. While
commonly attributed to forecast error or failures in operations, we posit that
this behavior can be explained from the perspective of risk-averse scheduling.
Using a stochastic self-scheduling framework and real-world data harvested from
the Australian National Electricity Market, we demonstrate that risk-averse
storage resources tend to have a myopic operational perspective, that is, they
typically engage in near-term price arbitrage and chase only few extreme price
spikes and troughs, thus remaining idle in several time periods with markedly
high and low prices. This has important policy implications given the
non-transparency of unit risk aversion and apparent risk in intervention
decision-making.
  From an ex-ante perspective, unit risk aversion can lead to a
risk-adjusted demand profile that is different from the forecasted one, which
can be exploited by resources to securely participate in the day-ahead
self-scheduling self-scheduling process. Importantly, we demonstrate that a
storage resource may avoid operating during times of extreme scarcity by
voluntarily shifting part of its risk to other resources. The presence of
risk aversion may lead to inter-market interactions that are not explicitly
coordinate among market operators. These interactions can influence the
day-ahead self-scheduling outcome in multiple ways, including by creating
opportunities for price manipulation. Our findings highlight the need for novel
risk-aware market monitoring and intervention strategies.

forecast error or failed start-up procedures. To quantify the difference between
these two sources of variability, we define a novel start-up success metric

estimate the contribution of unit risk aversion from the total risk exposure of
the market. Finally, we explore risk-adjusted demand profiles and their
implications for market operators, highlighting how risk aversion can be
exploited by resources to securely participate in the day-ahead self-scheduling
process. A suitable adjustment of risk estimates can minimize the impact of
risk aversion on market analysis and assessment, enabling monitoring of units

to evaluate the effectiveness of AL+SSP on datasets of interest. Our framework
takes as input a pool of misclassified samples and a function to estimate sample
difficulty. We demonstrate that this framework can be used to understand the
effective search strategy used by both random and interactive AL algorithms.

scenarios. We show that ACN protocol offers an important gain in terms of
fairness over other existing protocols.

formulation of DP in the context of graph-structured data is difficult, as

conclude our work with an overview of the current state of the art, difficulties
and future directions, highlighting the need for more research in this area.

for non-holonomic robots
moving at constant linear speeds in the 2-D plane is considered. The maneuvers
to avoid collisions are designed using dynamic vortex potential fields (PFs)
and their negative gradients; this formulation leads to a reciprocal behaviour
between the robots, denoted as being cooperative. The repulsive field is
selected as a function of the velocity and position of a robot relative to
another and introducing vorticity in its definition guarantees the absence of
local minima. Such a repulsive field is activated by a robot only when it is on
a collision path with other mobile robots or stationary obstacles. By analysing
the kinematics-based engagement dynamics in polar coordinates, it is shown that
a cooperative robot is able to avoid collisions with non-cooperating robots,
such as stationary and constant velocity robots, as well as those actively
seeking to collide with it. Conditions on the PF parameters are identified that
ensure collision avoidance for all cases. Experimental results acquired using a
mobile robot platform support the theoretical contributions.
  A novel approach to mobile robot collision avoidance is presented, which enables robots to avoid collisions with non-cooperating robots, such as stationary and constant velocity robots, as well as those actively seeking to collide with it.
Conditions on the field parameters are identified that ensure collision avoidance for all cases.
The proposed approach does not require any form of communication between robots, which is often required in other collision avoidance methods.
Moreover, the proposed method does not require any form of prediction of the trajectories of non-cooperating robots, which is often needed in motion planning algorithms to avoid collisions.
Instead, the proposed method relies on the activation of a repulsive field by a robot only when it is on a collision path with other mobile robots or stationary obstacles.
By analysing the kinematics-based engagement dynamics in polar coordinates, it is shown that a cooperating robot is able to avoid collisions with non-cooperating robots, thus guaranteeing a safe operation.
Experimental results acquired using a mobile robot platform support the theoretical contributions.
  Future work will consider extending the proposed approach to the collision avoidance problem for robots moving at non-constant linear speeds.
Additionally, the proposed approach will be extended to consider cooperating robots moving in three-dimensional space.
  Keywords: potential fields, non-holonomic robots, mobile robot collision avoidance, cooperative robots, reciprocal behaviour.

performance of machine learning models, allowing model selection and parameter
tuning. However, the very process of CV requires random partitioning of the
data and so our performance estimates are in fact stochastic, with variability
that can be substantial for natural language processing tasks. We demonstrate
that these unstable estimates cannot be relied upon for effective parameter
tuning. The resulting tuned parameters are highly sensitive to how our data is
partitioned, meaning that we often select sub-optimal parameter choices and
have serious reproducibility issues.
  Instead, we propose to use robustness to provide a reliable measure of
performance that is not sensitive to the particular partition used. We define
a robust CV estimate as the sample of means across many CV folds, with
sample size determined by the "cost" of estimating performance on each training
data set (measured by the number of examples left over for testing). We
demonstrate that this simple approach yields performance estimates that are
variance stable, allows effective tuning on a single run, and is compatible
with popular deep learning architectures for sentiment classification and
machine translation.

for deep learning models. Instead, we estimate performance on large sets of

an understudied area. Here we investigate how public sector officials
self-assess their dependency on the Google Web search engine, whether they are
aware of the potential impact of algorithmic biases on their ability to
retrieve all relevant information, and how much relevant information may
actually be missed due to Web search personalisation. We find that the majority
of participants in our survey (1) acknowledge the potential impact of
algorithmic biases, (2) are however not sure how to mitigate such biases, and
(3) may in fact miss up to $39\%$ of all relevant web pages.
  We demonstrate the latter by means of a follow-up experiment with the same
participants. We show that, on topics of public interest, automated searches
by
 artificial grapple accounts miss $17\%$ of the web pages that are found by
human searchers who are aware of the automated nature of the search. This
amounts to an average of $41.6$ potentially missed web pages per search.
This
underlines the importance of awareness and the need for training that allows
web search users to effectively deal with algorithmic biases and
personalisation in order to find all relevant information.
  In order to assist web search users interested in finding all relevant
information, we provide two tools. First, we offer a bookmarklet that temporarily
disables personalisation when clicked. Second, we release a dataset of
high-quality, fully de-identified search logs that have been checked for
sensitivity by an expert. Both can be used to raise awareness, to train search
engine models that can find all relevant information and to conduct further
research on algorithmic biases and Web search personalisation.
  In summary, our study underlines the need for awareness, clear guidelines and
possibly regulatory action among the major search engines to assess and mitigate
algorithmic biases and personalisation.

algorithmic biases on the search for scientific information, i.e., what is
considered essential knowledge in a particular field of science.
Moreover, future parities should investigate whether there are groups of
Web search users who are disproportionately affected by algorithmic biases and
what the societal implications are.

algorithmic biases and personalisation combined.

application to radiology and MR-guided radiotherapy.
  Methods: k-space data are continuously acquired in an interleaved manner
using two low-resolution matching pulses (LPs) with different resonance
frequencies (RFs) at a small B$_1$-field inhomogeneity, one centered at the
population's average respiratory frequency (RF1) and the other shifted 0.05
Hz higher (RF2). Synchronized acquisition is achieved by alternating the
switching of the (different) transverse LPs after the excitation pulse,
depending on the respiratory phase. The four-fold RPE is achieved by
acquiring two matching pulses with k-space data symmetrical about the
respiration cycle (one after the excitation pulse and the other inserted between
the two transverse LPs). The reconstruction involves three-dimensional
complex conjugate image subtraction. This motion-compensated 4D MRSI approach
was evaluated both in vitro (phantoms with gelatinous polycyanoacrylate
inclusions) and in vivo in rats with application to MR-guided radiotherapy.
  Results: The proposed 4D MRSI achieved high spatial and spectral
resolutions. The typical temporal resolution was 1.4/s, and the typical
four-dimensional image reconstruction time was 5.5/min. Clear
respiration-induced $T_2$-weighted contrast was observed in the in vitro
experiments, while in vivo, the proposed 4D MRSI allowed for the detection of
tumors and tracking of their motion and shape. The use of only two low-resolution
matching pulses per excitation reduced the total RPE efficiency by approximately
25% compared to a classical RPE scheme with four matching pulses, at the cost
of some reduced compensation capability.
  Conclusion: The proposed 3D+respiration MRSI sequence offers promising
capabilities for radiology and MR-guided radiotherapy, while allowing for
continuous MR-guidance at high spatial and spectral resolutions.

violated. We also find that when the usual attractor does not operate, kicks

Existing methods typically insert actors into the scene according to a set of
hand-crafted heuristics and are limited in their ability to model the true
complexity and diversity of real traffic scenes, thus inducing a content gap
between synthesized traffic scenes versus real ones. As a result, existing
simulators lack the fidelity necessary to train and test self-driving vehicles.
To address this limitation, we present SceneGen, a neural autoregressive model
of traffic scenes that eschews the need for rules and heuristics. In
particular, given the ego-vehicle state and a high definition map of
surrounding area, SceneGen inserts actors of various classes into the scene and
synthesizes their sizes, orientations, and velocities. We demonstrate on two
large-scale datasets SceneGen's ability to faithfully model distributions of
real traffic scenes. Moreover, we show that SceneGen coupled with sensor
simulation can be used to train perception models that generalize to the real
world.
  From a technical standpoint, SceneGen is a conditionally spatial autoregressive
generative model that models the probability distribution over traffic scenes.
While high-dimensional, SceneGen's input representation -- the map -- has a
lower-dimensional representation than prior autoregressive generation models.
To account for this, SceneGen employs a novel spatial RNN architecture that
effectively exploits the map to condition the probability distribution to the
ego-vehicle state. As a result, SceneGen is orders of magnitude faster than
multiplying out all possible actor configurations. We demonstrate that SceneGen
maintains generation quality while increasing performance by more than 5x on a
high-performance GPU.
  Finally, we stress that SceneGen is not just a generation model, but a
simulation model that can be used to train and validate perception models.
Specifically, we show that SceneGen can be coupled with sensor simulation to
produce a validation distribution that closely matches the real validation
distribution.

simulating the evolution of electronic states as the nuclear positions change
requires a quantum-classical interface that can handle moving nuclei. Here, we
show that it is possible to use machine learning to reconstruct the PES of a
molecule from simulations of its quantum state at different nuclear

outcomes of these simulations and find that the errors are significantly
reduced compared to other methods. Importantly, our method can be applied to

configuration.

quantitatively compare with density functional theory. Moreover, we can
determine the optimal reaction pathway and the corresponding energetic profile
that is expected from a density functional calculation. While machine learning
is used to study one nuclear coordinate at a time, it greatly reduces the
computation time and allows us to study very slow reactions that would be
prohibitive with current first-principles methods. Finally, we show that a single
network can be used to classify the energetic outcomes for a range of
density-functional approximations, suggesting that quantum machine learning
techniques will be invaluable for reducing the scale of 21st century density

a novel technique for automatically
learning system call filtering policies for containerized microservices
applications. At run-time, Timeloops automatically learns which system calls a
program should be allowed to invoke while rejecting attempts to call spurious
system calls. Further, Timeloops addresses many of the shortcomings of
state-of-the-art static analysis-based techniques, such as the ability to
generate tight filters for programs written in interpreted languages such as
PHP, Python, and JavaScript. Timeloops has a simple and robust implementation
because it is mainly built out of commodity, and proven, technologies such as
seccomp-BPF, systemd, and Podman containers, with fewer than 500 lines of code.
We demonstrate the utility of Timeloops by learning system calls for individual
services and two microservices benchmark applications, which utilize popular
technologies like Python Flask, Nginx (with PHP and Lua modules), Apache
Thrift, Memcached, Redis, and MongoDB. Further, the amortized performance of
Timeloops is similar to that of an unhardened system while producing a smaller
system call filter than state-of-the-art static analysis-based techniques.
Finally, we show that Timeloops can be effectively integrated with
fail-make-harm, a recently introduced resilience composition framework, to
produce hard failure assumptions that preserve functional correctness.
Fail-make-harm calls system calls whose filters are tightly coupled with the
programs they protect, which is exactly the kind of system calls that
Timeloops learns to allow (or reject) for microservices applications.

communication coexistence (DED2D) system. The DED2D system allows a base
station (BS) to transfer data to information-demanded users (IUs) and energy to
energy-demanded users (EUs), i.e., using a time-fraction-based (TFB) and
power-fraction-based (PFB) mode, respectively. Furthermore, the DED2D system
allows D2D communication to share spectrum with the BS. Therefore, the DED2D
system can improve spectrum utilization and energy efficiency. However, the
DED2D system faces interference from D2D transmissions to IUs and EUs, which
degrades the system's performance. To deal with this issue, we propose and
analyze interference-free modes for the DED2D system. We then obtain the
throughput and energy transfer rate of the DED2D system for each interference-free
mode. Next, we maximize the sum of the DED2D system's throughput and energy
transfer rate under the interference-free modes. The optimization problem is
non-convex and can be solved by using discrete reinforcement to continue the
optimization (RRCO) and dynamic programming. However, the RRCO approach has a
delay problem when using a finite number of time slots. Therefore, we propose
an improved RRCO protocol (IRRP) to overcome the delay problem. The IRRP
calculates the optimal time and power fractions for the TFB and PFB modes,
respectively, in advance and stores the results in a look-up table. Then, we
only need a small amount of time to determine the time and power fractions for
the IRRP. Therefore, the IRRP is much faster than the RRCO protocol when using a
finite number of time slots. Simulation results show that the IRRP produces
results similar to those of the RRCO protocol in a few time slots and is much
faster and more efficient than the RRCO protocol when using a large number of time
slots.

TESS have demonstrated that
planets are ubiquitous. However, the success of these missions heavily depends
on ground-based radial velocity (RV) surveys, which combined with transit
photometry can yield bulk densities and orbital properties. While most Kepler
host stars are too faint for detailed follow-up observations, TESS is detecting
planets orbiting nearby bright stars that are more amenable to RV
characterization. Here we introduce the TESS-Keck Survey (TKS), an RV program
using ~100 nights on Keck/HIRES to study exoplanets identified by TESS. The
primary survey aims are investigating the link between stellar properties and
the compositions of small planets; studying how the diversity of system
architectures depends on dynamical configurations or planet multiplicity;
identifying prime candidates for atmospheric studies with JWST; and
understanding the role of stellar evolution in shaping planetary systems. We
present a fully-automated target selection algorithm, which yielded 103 planets
in 86 systems for the final TKS sample. Most TKS hosts are inactive,
solar-like, main-sequence stars (4500 K < Teff < 6000 K) at a wide range of
metallicities. The selected TKS sample contains 71 small planets (Rp < 4 Re),
11 systems with multiple transiting candidates, 6 sub-day period planets and 3
planets in orbits < 0.01 AU. The TKS sample is representative of the population
of small planet systems identified by TESS, with ~55% of in-sample planets having
periods within the range 1-10 days. Follow-up observations with this sample are
vital for fully exploiting the scientific value of the TESS planetary systems
detection population.

  In the last decades, the gaming industry has experienced a tremendous growth.

industry, with revenues surpassing those of other well-known segments of the
digital industry (market research). Due to its economic importance, the gaming
industry has attracted the attention of several academic areas, including that
of requirements engineering. This area of research has the potential of
contributing significantly to the improvement of the quality of gaming products
and, as a consequence, of their quality in general. However, a first step in
this direction, that of understanding the background and the current practices
in the area of requirements engineering in the gaming industry, has not yet been
completely undertaken. In fact, there are few papers on the matter found in the
literature. In this context, the aim of this work is to present an account of
the status of requirements engineering in the gaming industry through a survey of
recent papers in the area. Our characterization of the gaming industry is
deliberated upon by portraying its relations with the market industry. In
addition, some potential research directions in the area of requirements
engineering in the gaming industry are also mentioned. Our conclusions highlight
the potential of offering customized processes to the gaming industry, tailored
to the specific needs of the businesses involved in the market.

as a randomized algorithm, and we prove that the randomized mechanism composed
of the analysis tool and the learning algorithm is identical in distribution
to a randomized mechanism that only depends on the analysis tool. This allows
us to: (1) exchange the order of analysis and learning without affecting the
privacy guarantee; (2) develop a generic recipe for analyzing the privacy of

theoretical results and show that by tuning the hyperparameters and the privacy

better test accuracy than the required privacy guarantee, which indicates that
the analysis should be done on the learned model (with appropriate
hyperparameters) before we know the desired level of privacy. That is, the

learning algorithm, rather than a mechanism that adds extra cost to achieve the

these two components, then compute the residuals \Delta[X/H] from this
two-parameter fit. The rms residuals range from ~0.01-0.03 dex for the most
precisely measured APOGEE abundances to ~0.1 dex for Na, V, and Ce. The
correlations of residuals reveal a complex underlying structure, including a
correlated element group comprised of Ca, Na, Al, K, Cr, and Ce and a separate
group comprised of Ni, V, Mn, and Co. Selecting stars poorly fit by the
2-process model reveals a rich variety of physical outliers and sometimes
subtle measurement errors. Residual abundances allow comparison of populations
controlled for differences in metallicity and [\alpha/Fe]. Relative to the main
disk (R=3-13 kpc, |Z|<2 kpc), the thick disk (2<kpc|Z<3 kpc) has higher [Na/Ca],
lower [Mg/Ni], and similar [Cr/O] or marginally higher. The young (\lessapprox
680 Myr age), high-velocity ("high-V") population is enriched in Na, Mn, V,
Cr, and Ce but has no measurable age dispersion, suggesting either a single
supernova explosion or full mixing with the surrounding interstellar medium.
High-V populations defined in lower-age cohorts (790-1270 Myr, 1270-1760 Myr,
1760-2340 Myr) each have increasing enrichment in these "additional" elements
with increasing age. Young disk populations defined in the DR17 stellar

spread, which may trace the role of Type Ia SNe in the star formation process.

of disk abundance patterns and demonstrate their utility for exploring systematic

world.In China, COVID-19 has caused severe consequences. Moreover, online
rumors during the COVID-19 pandemic increased people's panic on public health
significantly. At present, understanding and curbing the spread of online rumors
have become an important task for preventing the pandemic's continuation and
its impact on society. This study proposes a novel framework for detecting
online rumors during the COVID-19 pandemic, which incorporates deep learning and
graph-based methods. In the framework, we first train a binary classification
model that combines a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Graph Convolutional
Network (GCN) for detecting online rumors. Next, we use another GCN model to
identify influential users who posted the rumors. We conduct experiments on a
dataset of tweets about the COVID-19 pandemic. The results show that our proposed
framework achieves higher accuracy compared to the baseline methods.
Therefor, the proposed framework is effective for detecting online rumors during
the COVID-19 pandemic.

to their host galaxies thanks to the nearly universal shape of the planetary
nebulae luminosity function (PNLF). Accurate PNe distance measurements rely on
obtaining well-sampled PNLFs and the number of observed PNe scales with the
encompassed stellar mass. This means either disposing of wide-field
observations or focusing on the bright central regions of galaxies. In this
work we take this second approach and conduct a census of the PNe population in
the central regions of galaxies in the Fornax cluster, using VLT/MUSE data for
the early-type galaxies observed over the course of the Fornax3D survey. Using
such integral-field spectroscopic observations to carefully separate the
nebular emission from the stellar continuum, we isolated [OIII] 5007 {\AA}
sources of interest, filtered out unresolved impostor sources or kinematic
outliers, and present a catalogue of 1350 unique PNe sources across 21
early-type galaxies, which includes their positions, [OIII] 5007 {\AA} line
magnitudes, and line-of-sight velocities. Using the PNe catalogued within each
galaxy, we present independently derived distance estimates based on the fit to
the entire observed PNLF observed while carefully accounting for the PNe
detection incompleteness and the effects on the derived distance estimate. We
obtain distance moduli which are on average only 0.035 mag away from the
median value and our estimates are highly consistent with previous Fornax3D
distance estimates based on the bright asymptotic giant branch (AGB) stars. We
furthermore show that including the PNe catalogued in this work as well as the
previous Fornax3D AGB-based distance estimates to the galaxies in the Fornax
cluster would greatly increase the dataset's statistical power, yielding a
much tighter determination of the cluster's global velocity dispersion, which
is only 0.35{\%} affected by the systematic offset present in the Tully-Fisher
relation. Finally, we discuss at what length-scales our sampled PNeLFs are
representative of the global galaxy PNeLFs and how this relates to the various
galaxy stellar mass components as defined by their H{\alpha} equivalent width
distribution.

important hyperparameters for a
neural network. Many loss functions have been designed to date, making a
correct choice nontrivial. However, elaborate justifications regarding the
choice of the loss function are not made in related work. This is, as we see
it, an indication of a dogmatic mindset in the deep learning community which
lacks empirical foundation. In this work, we consider deep neural networks in a
supervised classification setting and analyze the impact the choice of loss
function has onto the training result. While certain loss functions perform
suboptimally, our work empirically shows that under-represented losses such as
the KL Divergence can outperform the State-of-the-Art choices significantly,
highlighting the need to include the loss function as a tuned hyperparameter
rather than a fixed choice.
  Which losses should be considered is a prior problem. Naively considering all
possible losses incurs computational costs due to the sheer diversity of
losses. A more practical approach is to consider only those losses functionally
different, i.e., losses that are equivalent up to gradient compounding are of
no difference. While existing works consider first-order functional equivalent
losses, our work extends this observation to higher-order functional equivalent
losses. We observe a substantial reduction in the number of distinguishable loss
functions thereby streamlining hyperparameter tuning. We demonstrate the
practicality of our observation by designing a novel loss layer that learns a
combination of distinguishable losses, thereby avoiding the need to manually
tune individual losses. Our layer is shown to outperform State-of-the-Art
arrangements of losses.
  Overall, our work suggests a paradigmatic shift in the way deep learning
models are designed. By considering the loss as a learned layer, we open up the
possibility of directly training the entire model using a single optimization
problem. While our work focuses on classification, we find that unifying the
loss will also be beneficial in the regression setting, where it could
potentially improve the generalization performance.

strain-induced crystallization in unfilled polymers. This phenomenon

kinds of effects, the model proposed starts by introducing a triple
decomposition of the deformation gradient and furthermore uses thermodynamic
framework for material modeling based on the Coleman--Noll procedure and
minimum principle of the dissipation potential, which requires suitable
assumptions for the Helmholtz free energy and the dissipation potential. The
chosen setup yields evolution equations which are able to simulate the
formation and the degradation of crystalline regions accompanied by the
temperature change during a cyclic tensile test. The boundary value problem
corresponding to the described process includes the balance of linear momentum
and balance of energy and serves as a basis for the numerical implementation
within an FEM code. The~paper closes with the numerical examples showing the
microstructure evolution and temperature distribution for different material
samples.
  The numerical examples computed in the FEM code are compared with the
experimental results obtained via DSC (Differential Scanning Calorimetry) and
TMA (Thermomechanical Analysis) tests. The aim is to evidence the influence of
the deformation on the crystallization temperature as well as on the amount of
the formed crystals. Besides that the example computed for a polymer sample
exposed to a cyclic tension highlights the evolution of the crystal zones
together with the temperature change during one cycle.

constant traction velocity. The computed example shows that the strain-induced
crystallization together with the temperature evolution lead to the hardening
of the polymer curve similar to the one measured via TMA test for real materials.

the Reynolds number corresponds to an increase in the concentration near the
down-stream seats. We filter the aerosol concentration field to study the
scale-dependent reduction in the concentration variance, which is important for
assessing the effectiveness of different mitigation strategies. Our results show

derive the error rate achieved by the computationally-intractable optimal

detector. We further validate our derivations through various numerical

optimal Bayesian detector is given by the sum of its spectral and non-spectral
components. We propose a simple scaling scheme to achieve the spectral part,
which is also feasible in a semi-distributed manner. Regarding the
non-spectral component, we propose a prediction-based tuning scheme for the
regularized detectors. We show that it outperforms the existing tuning
strategies significantly, while being computationally trivial. Numerical
experiments illustrate that our scheme can yield an order of magnitude gain in
distortion reduction.

transmit rate achieved by means of linear zero-forcing and linear jammer
prevention, under both blind and trained channel estimation. This provides a
comprehensive characterization of the performance of massive spatial modulation
MIMO systems.

signal-to-noise ratio, rather than by increasing the number of antennas.

detector does not guarantee optimal performance when the distortion function is

Communication), for studying goal-driven and grounded natural language
interactions. Specifically, we choose Dungeons and Dragons (D&D) -- a
role-playing game consisting of multiple player characters and a Dungeon Master
(DM) who collaborate to achieve a set of goals that are beneficial to the
players -- as a testbed for this task. Here, each of the player characters is a
student, with their own personas and abilities, and the DM is the teacher, an
arbitrator of the rules of the world and responsible for assisting and guiding
the students towards a global goal. We propose a theory-of-mind-inspired
methodology for training such a DM with reinforcement learning (RL), where a
DM: (1) learns to predict how the players will react to its utterances using a
dataset of D&D dialogue transcripts; and (2) uses this prediction as a reward
function providing feedback on how effective these utterances are at guiding
the players towards a goal. Human and automated evaluations show that a DM
trained with RL to generate guidance by incorporating a theory-of-mind of the
players significantly improves the players' ability to achieve goals grounded
in their shared world.
  We release a theory-of-mind-inspired dataset of 1,500 D&D dialogue transcripts
derived from 300 hours of audio, as well as a RL baseline framework that
demonstrates the effectiveness of theory-of-mind-empowered language policies in
grounded multi-agent tasks. This resource can be used to study other aspects
of multi-agent groundings and theory-of-mind-inspired language policies, as
well as be a testbed for evaluating AI systems designed to play D&D and similar
games that require high levels of collaboration between agents.

organization behind D&D, which permits the release of transcripts but

process is an open and challenging question in biology. Recent studies classify
the topology and geometry of knotted proteins by analysing the distribution of
a protein's planar projections using topological objects called knotoids. We
approach the analysis of proteins with the same topology by introducing a
topologically inspired statistical metric between their knotoid distributions.
We detect geometric differences between trefoil proteins by characterising
their entanglement and we recover a clustering by sequence similarity. By
looking directly at the geometry and topology of their native states, we are
able to probe different folding pathways for proteins forming open-ended
trefoil knots. Interestingly, our pipeline reveals that the folding pathway of
shallow knotted Carbonic Anhydrases involves the creation of a double-looped
structure, differently from what was previously observed for deeply knotted
trefoil proteins. We validate this with Molecular Dynamics simulations.
Moreover, we observe that the shallowness of the knoting in the Glucosylceramidase
folding pathway is induced by the accumulation of disordered regions at the C
terminus that prevent the creation of a double-looped structure. Our results
provide a new insight on how proteins can be topologically and geometrically
organized to perform specific functions, and how topology can influence the
protein design.
  From a mathematical perspective, our approach relies on recent results in
topology of planes equipped with metrics that measure the distance between knotoid
representations. We leverage on the connection between knotoid distances and
classical topological invariants, to define a suitable statistical metric to
compare knotoid distributions. This allows us to depart from the comparison
between single proteins and give a general characterisation of proteins forming
open-ending trefoil knots. Moreover, our method can be used on any kind of data
coded in knotoids, not only protein structures. We can consider different
geometric features of proteins by changing the generating set of the knotoid
topology, providing a flexible framework for data analysis.

energy (EDE), is a proposed solution to the Hubble tension. Currently, there is
no consensus in the literature as to whether EDE can simultaneously solve the
Hubble tension and provide an adequate fit to the data from the cosmic
microwave background (CMB) and large-scale structure of the universe. In this
work, we deconstruct the current constraints from Planck CMB and the
full-shape clustering data of the Baryon Oscillation Spectroscopic Survey
(BOSS) to understand the origin of different conclusions in the literature. We
use two different analyses to address this question: a rejection sampler and a
traditional Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampler. In the future, high
precision clustering data from DESI will be able to directly see the EDE
signal. However, given the current state of the art, we find that the
compatibility of an EDE model with observations depends on the methodology used
to analyse the data. Therefore, we argue that future works studying this model
should not only be based on a large volume of data, but also should thoroughly
investigate the assumption implicit in the analytical methods. Furthermore,
we suggest a simple way to increase the volume of usable data by marginalizing
over the present day value of the Hubble constant, rather than fixing it to its
most recent precise measurement.

  A key input in the proof of the adjunction property of GNS is the following
new result: any cyclic representation of a C*-algebra carries the information
of the unit vector with which it is coupled. More formally, if $\pi$ is a
representation of a C*-algebra $\mathcal{A}$ and $\phi$ is a unit vector in the
Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_\pi$ acted upon by $\pi$, then there exists another
representation $\pi'$ of $\mathcal{A}$ such that $\pi'_\phi \simeq \pi$ and
$\pi'_\psi \perp \phi$ for all other unit vectors $\psi$ on $\mathcal{H}_{\pi'}$.
This result for GNS representations is equivalent to the existence of conditional
states on $\mathcal{A}$, which in turn is equivalent to the existence of
quantum maximal (or minimal) relative entropy on $\mathcal{A}$. A discussion
on the physical importance of conditional states and the related notion of
relative entropy is included.

category of GNS representations of C*-algebras together with unit vectors. This
equivalence of categories extends to the larger category of W*-algebras, where
a unit vector is replaced by a cyclic and separating vector.

modeling the distribution of portfolio returns across portfolios. We establish
relevant mathematical formulas and propose efficient algorithms, drawing upon
powerful techniques in computational geometry and the literature on splines, to
compute the probability density function, the cumulative distribution function,
and the k-th moment of the probability function. Our algorithmic tools and

assessment of portfolio concentration, the construction of tail-risk measures,

  In this paper, we develop the theoretical foundation behind our framework for
modeling the distribution of portfolio returns across portfolios. There are three
core concepts that are central to our framework: the equity spline, the
coefficient curve, and the portfolio return distribution. We establish the
theoretical properties behind each of these concepts and demonstrate how they are
interconnected. This is the foundation upon which our algorithms for computing
portfolios concentration, tail-risk measures, and systemic risk are built.
  In this paper, we illustrate the effectiveness of our models and algorithms
through three numerical examples and a case study. In Examples 1-2, we demonstrate
how our framework can be applied to different sectors of the stock market. In
Example 3, we show how our algorithms can be used to assess concentration and
systemic risk in portfolios constructed from stocks across the different
sectors. In the case study, we apply our framework to a dataset of stock prices
published by Standard \& Poor's (S\&P) and demonstrate how our measures can be
used to monitor portfolio performance relative to market performance.
  In this paper, we present two algorithms that can be used to assess the
distribution of portfolio returns across portfolios. The first algorithm can be
used to compute the probability density function, the cumulative distribution
function, and the k-th moment of the probability function. The second algorithm
can be used to sort portfolios according to their concentration, tail-risk
measures, and systemically important portfolios. We present efficient
implementations of these algorithms and draw upon powerful techniques in
computational geometry to reduce their computational time by up to 1000 times.

smart phones and wristbands make it easy to get access to people's health
information including activities, sleep, sports, etc. Smart healthcare achieves
great success by training machine learning models on a large quantity of user
data. However, there are two critical challenges. Firstly, user data often
exists in the form of isolated islands, making it difficult to perform
aggregation without compromising privacy security. Secondly, the models trained
on the cloud fail on personalization. In this paper, we propose FedHealth, the
first federated transfer learning framework for wearable healthcare to tackle
these challenges. FedHealth performs data aggregation through federated
learning, and then builds personalized models by transfer learning. It is able
to achieve accurate and personalized healthcare without compromising privacy
and security. Experiments demonstrate that FedHealth produces higher accuracy
(5.3\% improvement) for wearable activity recognition when compared to
traditional methods. FedHealth is general and extensible and has the potential
to be used in many healthcare applications.
  We propose a novel framework to perform activity recognition on a wearable
device. Unlike existing approaches that rely on sensor data, our framework
predicts activity by analyzing the energy consumption pattern of the device.
Since the energy pattern is device specific, our framework can effectively
disambiguate activities that produce similar sensor signals. It also has the
advantage of not requiring massive labeled data to achieve high accuracy. With
labeled data from $200$ minutes of walking, jogging, and running, our experiment
shows an average recognition accuracy of $92.3\%$.

  As the smart grid becomes more complex, the need for frequent and extensive
testing increases. Therefore, the use of simulation tools becomes essential.
However, the development of a simulation platform from scratch is challenging.
This paper shows that it is possible to speed up the development of a simulation
platform for a real-world system, such as the Australian energy market, using a
modular design. The design consists of a set of interconnected microservices
that are easy to develop, test, and deploy. We demonstrate a simulation of a
market clearing mechanism in Australia, showing that the simulation reaches a

identifying the presence of a malicious agent in a system. The methodology
combines a new learning-based feature engineering mechanism with a robust

designed to capture the notion of "similarities" in the time-series data generated
by a malicious agent. Our experiments show that the proposed test significantly
outperforms the state-of-the-art methods. We also show that the proposed
methodology can be used to identify the presence of malicious agents in multiple

experiment our approach on 12 real-world datasets. The results show that the
results are significant and superior to the state-of-the-art methods.

the changes of regimes is allowed to have discontinuities in time. While for
continuous costs the optimal strategy is characterized by means of upper and
lower value functions which are both harmonic, for discontinuous costs the
optimal strategy requires the definition of an additional function, namely the
skipping value function, which is a superharmonic function. These functions
are well known in the control community but, to the best of our knowledge, the
connection with the theory of Dirichlet problems for discontinuous functions
has not been established yet. We establish the necessary and sufficient
conditions for the existence of solutions to Dirichlet problems for
discontinuous functions and we prove that the skipping value function is a
solution to the corresponding boundary value problem. Therefore, by combining
the results of the theory of Dirichlet problems with those of switching control
problems, we provide a new characterization of the optimal strategy which
combines the advantages of both theories.

accuracy and significant decrease mistake severity on instrument classes unseen
in training.

  Let $X$ be a projective algebraic variety of dimension $d \geq 2$ over an
algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic zero. The (quasi-)projective
variety $M_{\geq p}$ parametrizes the based stable maps of genus $p \to X$ of
degree $b$ and is constructed via gluing quasiprojective spaces along
lower-dimensional subspaces. As $M_{\geq p}$ is not compact, Falk and
Flenner have defined its compactification $\overline{M}_{\geq p}$ as the
Hodge-theoretic compactification, i.e. it is the closure of the image of the
inclusion $M_{\geq p} \hookrightarrow \overline{\mathrm{M}}_{\geq p}$ in the
Deligne-Mumford compactification $\overline{\mathrm{M}}_{\geq p}$. This
notion generalizes to other moduli problems such as stratabic moduli and
map-moduli.
  We review the general construction of Hodge-theoretic compactifications,
their relationship with Geometric Invariant Theory (GIT) stable varieties,
their generalization to other invariant theoretic problems and the connection
with motivic invariant theory. We also survey the current state of research
for compactifications of specific moduli spaces such as those of curves, surfaces
and higher dimensional varieties.
  Finally, we survey the generalities of the relationship between GIT
stable varieties and the algebraic Kähler--Einstein equations, and how the
latter generalizes to other invariant theoretic problems.
  Last, we survey recent results on the existence of Hodge-theoretic
compactifications for moduli spaces of algebraic varieties defined over
non-algebraically closed fields.

recognition in the dark.
In this work, we present our results on the ARID dataset. Most previous works
only evaluate performance on large, well illuminated datasets like Kinetics and
HMDB51. We demonstrate that our work is able to achieve a very low error rate
while being trained on a much smaller dataset of dark videos. We also explore a
variety of training and inference strategies including domain transfer
methodologies and also propose a simple but useful frame selection strategy.
Our empirical results demonstrate that we beat previously published baseline
models by 11%.
  We also investigate the efficacy of two domain transfer strategies (the
cycleGAN and the adversarial domain specific model) to improve the model's
ability to recognize actions in dark videos. We observe that while these
methods do improve performance, they are however computationally expensive.
Thus, we propose a simple but effective frame selection strategy to reduce the
computational cost while maintaining a very low error rate. We find that for every
30% reduction in computational cost, we can maintain the same validation
accuracy by selectively rejecting up to 40% of the frames.
  Finally, we also investigate the effect of training with noise to improve our
model's robustness. We find that by simply augmenting the training videos with
noise, we can significantly improve our model's resistance to noise.
  In summary, our work demonstrates that we are able to achieve a very low
error rate (11%) on the ARID dataset that benchmarks supervised action
recognition in dark videos. We also propose a variety of techniques including
domain transfer strategies and a simple but useful frame selection strategy.
Our empirical results demonstrate that these techniques are able to significantly
improve performance while reducing the computational cost.

is compensated for by the fact that it can be built with a fairly small FPGA.

operations as well as the combinators can be used to solve simple problems, and
how the CAPP can be wrapped in a higher-level parallel processing framework.

construction of a fully-fledged parallel computer.

commitment schemes: a compelled commitment scheme is a compelled act that

revised to reflect the rights and freedoms of the user. That is, security can
be expressed in terms of the autonomy of the user.

collecting large datasets from emerging treatments such as LITT is impractical.
In this paper, we propose a progressive brain lesion synthesis framework
(PAVAE) to expand both the quantity and diversity of the training dataset.
Concretely, our framework consists of two sequential networks: a mask synthesis
network and a mask-guided lesion synthesis network. To better employ extrinsic
information to provide additional supervision during network training, we
design a condition embedding block (CEB) and a mask embedding block (MEB) to
encode inherent conditions of masks to the feature space. Finally, a
segmentation network is trained using raw and synthetic lesion images to
evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed framework. Experimental results show
that our method can achieve a comparable performance to the state-of-the-art
method using only real images at test time.
  We believe our framework to be general and may be applied to other deep
learning-based methods that require more high-quality synthetic data.
Furthermore, our framework can be transferred to other emerging treatments to
assist with tissue segmentation.

regions relevant to Parkinson's Disease based on local field potential data
collected from the brain of marmoset monkeys. Parkinson's disease is a
neurodegenerative disorder, linked to the death of dopaminergic neurons at the
substantia nigra pars compacta, which affects the normal dynamics of the basal
ganglia-thalamus-cortex neuronal circuit of the brain. Although there are
multiple mechanisms underlying the disease, a complete description of those
mechanisms and molecular pathogenesis are still missing, and there is still no
cure. To address this gap, computational models that resemble neurobiological
aspects found in animal models have been proposed. In our model, we performed a
data-driven approach in which a set of biologically constrained parameters is
optimised using differential evolution. Evolved models successfully resembled
single-neuron mean firing rates and spectral signatures of local field
potentials from healthy and parkinsonian marmoset brain data. As far as we are
concerned, this is the first computational model of Parkinson's Disease based
on simultaneous electrophysiological recordings from seven brain regions of
Marmoset monkeys. Results show that the proposed model could facilitate the
investigation of the mechanisms of PD and support the development of techniques
that can indicate new therapies. It could also be applied to other
computational neuroscience studies.
  We provide an open-source Python implementation of this model which can be
utilised to explore Parkinson's Disease further. In addition, we make available
a dedicated website that permits the interactive visualisation and comparison
of simulated data from the proposed model with experimental data
supporting its development. This is the first time that we are aware of an
interactive visualisation of electrophysiological recordings from seven brain
regions of Marmoset monkeys being made available.
  Overall, the proposed model has the potential to contribute to the
development of techniques that can indicate new therapies for Parkinson's
Disease. It can also be utilised to explore other computational neuroscience
studies in detail.

incremental cost and limited scope. To ensure smooth operation of all

this problem is that weather conditions are diverse in nature and there is an

classification of two categories of weather. In this paper, we have created a
new open source dataset consisting of images depicting three classes of weather

proposed which has used super pixel delimiting masks as a form of data
augmentation, leading to reasonable results with respect to ten Convolutional
